# CLAUDE.md — Papaya DevSecOps Challenge 1

## Purpose of this repo

This repository is my submission for Papaya's **DevSecOps Challenge 1 — "DevSecOps with
Coding Agents at Papaya"** (full text: `work/00-challenge.md`). The task is to design the
framework and workflow for how Papaya uses coding agents (Claude Code) for DevSecOps,
reconciling two positions:

- Engineering: "Let Claude Code talk to AWS directly."
- Compliance: "Nothing changes in production without a named human who reviewed and approved it."

Two things make this repo unusual and shape every rule below:

1. **The complete, raw Claude Code session transcripts are part of the submission** and are
   graded. Work transparently: state the reason behind each recommendation, show trade-offs,
   and say so when something is unverified.
2. **I have no access to Papaya's systems or code**, and the challenge does not expect it.
   Everything is a design on top of the stack described in the challenge's Appendix A.

## Hard constraints from the brief

- Design for Papaya's existing stack: AWS (Lambda via Serverless Framework, ECS, EC2, Aurora
  PostgreSQL, SNS/SQS, Step Functions, S3, CloudWatch), GCP (Vertex AI, Gemini), k0s
  Kubernetes, Firebase Hosting, a single GitHub monorepo, GitHub Actions, Pulumi, Claude Code
  (Team Premium) with an internal plugin marketplace, Linear, Slack.
- **Do not propose replacing IaC or CI tooling** (no "switch Pulumi to Terraform", no "move off
  GitHub Actions"). Improve how they are used.
- Compliance context: ISO 27001 (in progress), HIPAA, regional data-protection law; multiple
  insurer tenants in different countries. Sensitive data: medical records, national IDs, bank
  accounts.

## Repository layout

| Path | Contents | Language |
|---|---|---|
| `README.md` | Entry point for graders: what the deliverable is, how to read it | English |
| `docs/` | The deliverable: framework, workflows, policies, rollout plan | English |
| `examples/` | Concrete, copy-pasteable artifacts: Claude Code settings/hooks, GitHub Actions workflows, IAM/OIDC policy sketches, plugin manifests | English |
| `diagrams/` | Architecture and workflow diagrams (source + rendered) | English labels |
| `work/` | Working notes, the challenge text (`00-challenge.md`), scratch analysis, decision log | Vietnamese or English |
| `transcripts/` | Copies of the raw Claude Code session files (`*.jsonl`) for this project, unedited | n/a |
| `CLAUDE.md` | This file | English |

Numbered prefixes (`00-`, `01-`, …) in `docs/` and `work/` define reading order. Running logs
that are not part of the reading order stay unnumbered (e.g. `work/session-log.md`).

## Rule 1 — Every claim about a tool's capability needs a source marker

The deliverable depends on what Claude Code, GitHub Actions, AWS IAM, Pulumi, k0s etc. can
actually do. Model memory is often stale. Therefore every non-trivial statement about a
feature, flag, setting, default, or limit carries one of these markers:

| Marker | Meaning | Required evidence |
|---|---|---|
| ✅ | Verified in this environment | A command run in this session with its output, or a file read here |
| 📖 | Taken from official documentation | A link to the specific doc page, ideally with the version/date |
| ⚠️ | Assumption or recollection, not verified | Say what would be needed to verify it |

Rules of use:

- Never present ⚠️ content as fact. If an assumption is load-bearing for a recommendation,
  flag it in the document as an open item to verify.
- Prefer ✅ over 📖 over ⚠️. If something can be checked locally (e.g. a Claude Code setting
  on this machine), check it.
- Keep markers in the submitted docs too, not only in work notes. Graders should be able to
  see what was verified and what was not.
- When the official docs and memory disagree, docs win; note the discrepancy.
- Do not invent product features, settings keys, CLI flags, or IAM condition keys. If a
  needed capability cannot be confirmed, design around it or mark it as a dependency.

## Rule 2 — No secrets, no personal data

- No credentials, tokens, API keys, account IDs, ARNs with real account IDs, kubeconfigs,
  private keys, or `.env` contents anywhere in this repo or in the chat. Examples use obvious
  placeholders such as `<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>` or `123456789012`.
- No personal data about real people: no names of Papaya staff, no email addresses other than
  what git already records as commit author, no customer or partner data. The challenge's
  example data categories (medical documents, national IDs) are referenced only as categories.
- Transcripts are committed unedited, as the challenge requires, so **do not paste secrets
  or personal data into the chat in the first place**. Do not print environment variables,
  settings files, or shell history without redacting values. If this rule is accidentally
  broken, stop and tell the user immediately before continuing.
- The git author identity is set repo-locally (personal address) before the first push; all
  commits were rewritten to it while still unpushed. Do not change it further.
- Accepted exception (decided session 2, 2026-11-08): the committed transcripts contain the
  author's own work email addresses (from tool output and from the context Claude Code
  injects). They are kept unedited because the challenge requires raw transcripts; no other
  person's data is involved.

## Rule 3 — Language

- **Submitted material** (`README.md`, everything in `docs/`, `examples/`, `diagrams/`,
  commit messages, code comments) is in **English**.
- **Working notes** in `work/` may be in Vietnamese or English, but every working note starts
  with an `## English summary` section (about 5–10 lines) directly under its title, so graders
  can follow the reasoning without reading Vietnamese. The summary only restates what the note
  already says. (Agreed 2026-11-09.)
- In chat, reply in the language the user writes in (currently Vietnamese), keeping technical
  terms in English.
- This file overrides the global rule that writes handover docs in Vietnamese.

## Decisions taken so far

- **Scope and assumptions (2026-11-08):** confirmed in `work/01-problem-framing.md` §6
  (rounds 1–2). In short: non-prod holds synthetic data only; prod and non-prod are separate
  AWS accounts; security of agent-written code is in scope at the PR/CI-guardrail level;
  security of Papaya's production AI agents is out of scope (noted only); all prod changes
  are approved before they are applied, including during incidents (incident approval within
  15 min, 24/7).
- **Deliverable form (2026-11-08):** Markdown docs in `docs/` plus `examples/` artifacts that
  can be validated locally. The audience is a panel of Engineering and Compliance, so every
  control states its cost to engineers and its value to compliance.
- **Branch:** everything is on `master`; no `main` branch.
- **Permission mode:** session 1 ran in auto mode. From session 2 on, sessions run in the
  default permission mode so the transcripts show the way of working the deliverable
  recommends (the challenge names "permission prompts turned off" as a problem).
- **Clean config directory:** from session 2 on, Claude Code runs with
  `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-papaya`, built by `work/setup-clean-config.sh`. It contains only
  the DevOps kit and the personal global CLAUDE.md, and disables claude.ai skill/plugin sync
  and connectors. Reason: the transcript embeds the system prompt, which lists every loaded
  skill, plugin and connector; the default profile pulls those from the user's employer
  account. Session 1's transcript still contains them; this is accepted and documented.
- **Transcript copies:** sessions under the clean profile write to
  `~/.claude-papaya/projects/<encoded-repo-path>/`; the copy command in `README.md` covers
  both locations.
- **Chosen approach (2026-11-09):** A + D2' from `work/03-options.md` §9. The PR pipeline is
  the default path for every prod change, incidents included ("IaC first"). A JIT window is
  only a narrow, approved fallback when the PR path is unavailable; it is accepted as meeting
  the approval constraint only partially. Incident target: ≤ 30 min from decision to apply.

## Rule 4 — Working method

- Design, don't execute: this project needs no live infrastructure. Do not run cloud CLIs,
  `kubectl`, `pulumi`, or `serverless` against any real target. Local, read-only commands
  (reading docs, listing files, validating YAML/JSON, rendering diagrams) are fine.
- Keep the challenge's two voices (Engineering vs Compliance) in view; every control should
  say what it costs engineers and what it gives compliance.
- Record decisions and discarded options in `work/` so the reasoning survives the session.
- Research and design steps go through an independent reviewer (a fresh subagent given the file
  and the review criteria, not the author's conclusions): review → fix → re-review until no
  HIGH/MEDIUM findings remain; only then present the result to the user. (Agreed 2026-11-08.)
- Ask the user when a choice materially changes the deliverable; otherwise pick the sensible
  default, state it, and continue.
- Before finishing a session, remind the user to copy the current transcript into
  `transcripts/` (see `README.md` for the command).

Coding Agents at Papaya"** (full text: `work/00-challenge.md`). The task is to design the
framework and workflow for how Papaya uses coding agents (Claude Code) for DevSecOps,
reconciling two positions:

- Engineering: "Let Claude Code talk to AWS directly."
- Compliance: "Nothing changes in production without a named human who reviewed and approved it."

Two things make this repo unusual and shape every rule below:

1. **The complete, raw Claude Code session transcripts are part of the submission** and are
   graded. Work transparently: state the reason behind each recommendation, show trade-offs,
   and say so when something is unverified.
2. **I have no access to Papaya's systems or code**, and the challenge does not expect it.
   Everything is a design on top of the stack described in the challenge's Appendix A.

## Hard constraints from the brief

- Design for Papaya's existing stack: AWS (Lambda via Serverless Framework, ECS, EC2, Aurora
  PostgreSQL, SNS/SQS, Step Functions, S3, CloudWatch), GCP (Vertex AI, Gemini), k0s
  Kubernetes, Firebase Hosting, a single GitHub monorepo, GitHub Actions, Pulumi, Claude Code
  (Team Premium) with an internal plugin marketplace, Linear, Slack.
- **Do not propose replacing IaC or CI tooling** (no "switch Pulumi to Terraform", no "move off
  GitHub Actions"). Improve how they are used.
- Compliance context: ISO 27001 (in progress), HIPAA, regional data-protection law; multiple
  insurer tenants in different countries. Sensitive data: medical records, national IDs, bank
  accounts.

## Repository layout

| Path | Contents | Language |
|---|---|---|
| `README.md` | Entry point for graders: what the deliverable is, how to read it | English |
| `docs/` | The deliverable: framework, workflows, policies, rollout plan | English |
| `examples/` | Concrete, copy-pasteable artifacts: Claude Code settings/hooks, GitHub Actions workflows, IAM/OIDC policy sketches, plugin manifests | English |
| `diagrams/` | Architecture and workflow diagrams (source + rendered) | English labels |
| `work/` | Working notes, the challenge text (`00-challenge.md`), scratch analysis, decision log | Vietnamese or English |
| `transcripts/` | Copies of the raw Claude Code session files (`*.jsonl`) for this project, unedited | n/a |
| `CLAUDE.md` | This file | English |

Numbered prefixes (`00-`, `01-`, …) in `docs/` and `work/` define reading order. Running logs
that are not part of the reading order stay unnumbered (e.g. `work/session-log.md`).

## Rule 1 — Every claim about a tool's capability needs a source marker

The deliverable depends on what Claude Code, GitHub Actions, AWS IAM, Pulumi, k0s etc. can
actually do. Model memory is often stale. Therefore every non-trivial statement about a
feature, flag, setting, default, or limit carries one of these markers:

| Marker | Meaning | Required evidence |
|---|---|---|
| ✅ | Verified in this environment | A command run in this session with its output, or a file read here |
| 📖 | Taken from official documentation | A link to the specific doc page, ideally with the version/date |
| ⚠️ | Assumption or recollection, not verified | Say what would be needed to verify it |

Rules of use:

- Never present ⚠️ content as fact. If an assumption is load-bearing for a recommendation,
  flag it in the document as an open item to verify.
- Prefer ✅ over 📖 over ⚠️. If something can be checked locally (e.g. a Claude Code setting
  on this machine), check it.
- Keep markers in the submitted docs too, not only in work notes. Graders should be able to
  see what was verified and what was not.
- When the official docs and memory disagree, docs win; note the discrepancy.
- Do not invent product features, settings keys, CLI flags, or IAM condition keys. If a
  needed capability cannot be confirmed, design around it or mark it as a dependency.

## Rule 2 — No secrets, no personal data

- No credentials, tokens, API keys, account IDs, ARNs with real account IDs, kubeconfigs,
  private keys, or `.env` contents anywhere in this repo or in the chat. Examples use obvious
  placeholders such as `<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>` or `123456789012`.
- No personal data about real people: no names of Papaya staff, no email addresses other than
  what git already records as commit author, no customer or partner data. The challenge's
  example data categories (medical documents, national IDs) are referenced only as categories.
- Transcripts are committed unedited except for one mechanical redaction (see the last bullet),
  so **do not paste secrets or personal data into the chat in the first place**. Do not print environment variables,
  settings files, or shell history without redacting values. If this rule is accidentally
  broken, stop and tell the user immediately before continuing.
- The git author identity is set repo-locally (personal address) before the first push; all
  commits were rewritten to it while still unpushed. Do not change it further.
- Accepted exception (decided session 2, 2026-11-08): the committed transcripts contain the
  author's own work email addresses (from tool output and from the context Claude Code
  injects). They are kept unedited because the challenge requires raw transcripts; no other
  person's data is involved.

## Rule 3 — Language

- **Submitted material** (`README.md`, everything in `docs/`, `examples/`, `diagrams/`,
  commit messages, code comments) is in **English**.
- **Working notes** in `work/` may be in Vietnamese or English, but every working note starts
  with an `## English summary` section (about 5–10 lines) directly under its title, so graders
  can follow the reasoning without reading Vietnamese. The summary only restates what the note
  already says. (Agreed 2026-11-09.)
- In chat, reply in the language the user writes in (currently Vietnamese), keeping technical
  terms in English.
- This file overrides the global rule that writes handover docs in Vietnamese.

## Decisions taken so far

- **Scope and assumptions (2026-11-08):** confirmed in `work/01-problem-framing.md` §6
  (rounds 1–2). In short: non-prod holds synthetic data only; prod and non-prod are separate
  AWS accounts; security of agent-written code is in scope at the PR/CI-guardrail level;
  security of Papaya's production AI agents is out of scope (noted only); all prod changes
  are approved before they are applied, including during incidents (incident approval within
  15 min, 24/7).
- **Deliverable form (2026-11-08):** Markdown docs in `docs/` plus `examples/` artifacts that
  can be validated locally. The audience is a panel of Engineering and Compliance, so every
  control states its cost to engineers and its value to compliance.
- **Branch:** everything is on `master`; no `main` branch.
- **Permission mode:** session 1 ran in auto mode. From session 2 on, sessions run in the
  default permission mode so the transcripts show the way of working the deliverable
  recommends (the challenge names "permission prompts turned off" as a problem).
- **Clean config directory:** from session 2 on, Claude Code runs with
  `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-papaya`, built by `work/setup-clean-config.sh`. It contains only
  the DevOps kit and the personal global CLAUDE.md, and disables claude.ai skill/plugin sync
  and connectors. Reason: the transcript embeds the system prompt, which lists every loaded
  skill, plugin and connector; the default profile pulls those from the user's employer
  account. Session 1's transcript still contains them; this is accepted and documented.
- **Transcript copies:** sessions under the clean profile write to
  `~/.claude-papaya/projects/<encoded-repo-path>/`; the copy command in `README.md` covers
  both locations.
- **Chosen approach (2026-11-09):** A + D2' from `work/03-options.md` §9. The PR pipeline is
  the default path for every prod change, incidents included ("IaC first"). A JIT window is
  only a narrow, approved fallback when the PR path is unavailable; it is accepted as meeting
  the approval constraint only partially. Incident target: ≤ 30 min from decision to apply.

## Rule 4 — Working method

- Design, don't execute: this project needs no live infrastructure. Do not run cloud CLIs,
  `kubectl`, `pulumi`, or `serverless` against any real target. Local, read-only commands
  (reading docs, listing files, validating YAML/JSON, rendering diagrams) are fine.
- Keep the challenge's two voices (Engineering vs Compliance) in view; every control should
  say what it costs engineers and what it gives compliance.
- Record decisions and discarded options in `work/` so the reasoning survives the session.
- Research and design steps go through an independent reviewer (a fresh subagent given the file
  and the review criteria, not the author's conclusions): review → fix → re-review until no
  HIGH/MEDIUM findings remain; only then present the result to the user. (Agreed 2026-11-08.)
- Ask the user when a choice materially changes the deliverable; otherwise pick the sensible
  default, state it, and continue.
- Before finishing a session, remind the user to copy the current transcript into
  `transcripts/` (see `README.md` for the command).

# Papaya DevSecOps Challenge 1 — Coding Agents for DevSecOps

Submission for [DevSecOps Challenge 1](https://github.com/papaya-insurtech/pumpkin/blob/main/Hiring/DevSecOps_Challenges/DevSecOps_Challenge_1.md)
(local copy: [work/00-challenge.md](work/00-challenge.md)).

> Status: complete. "Owner" in these documents is the author of this submission, who approved each
> document while writing it; it is not a Papaya sign-off · Updated: 2026-11-09

## The problem and the answer

Engineering wants Claude Code to talk to AWS directly; Compliance wants nothing to change in
production without a named human who reviewed and approved it. The two only disagree about **writes
to production**: reads of metadata and all of non-prod are outside Compliance's sentence.

The answer (the author's proposal): **every prod change is a pull request**, approved by a code
owner who is not the author and applied by CI, incidents included. A time-boxed, approved JIT grant,
used by a human without an agent, is the only fallback during an incident when the PR path cannot be
used. Nobody, human or agent, holds standing prod write or long-lived credentials. Exceptions:
k0s/Firebase CI deploy credentials, kept as secrets of a separate `production-k0s` environment (OD1,
OD24); the Expo robot token and update-signing key, in a separate `production-mobile` environment
(OD40), because Expo has no keyless login from GitHub; and the private keys of the approval-gate and CI-agent GitHub Apps, kept in a secrets store
and rotated (G19).

| Engineering gets | Compliance gets |
|---|---|
| A free non-prod loop with the agent; read-only prod metadata | Approval **before** apply by a named human ≠ author, enforced by GitHub and AWS IAM, outside the agent |
| One approval (two on process paths and data fixes), same-day ship; incident approval ≤ 15 min, 24/7 | One evidence chain per change, kept 6 years under Object Lock from phase 1; target ≤ 30 min to retrieve it, realistic from phase 2 |
| **Costs:** slower incident lane (est. 11–46 min); from phase 2 the agent cannot push, open PRs, run Docker or reach a private registry without a workaround; from phase 1 every `aws`/`pulumi`/`serverless` call asks first, in auto mode too (OD43); raw logs of a service only after its masking lands (deadline: end of phase 2 for claims services); 24/7 approver duty; ≤ 5 days for a new tool | **It does not give:** a technical stop on an agent approving through its engineer's login (deny rules are hygiene, approvals are only flagged); a GitHub login tied to the identity provider (a register does it on Team); prevention of admins editing the gate (logged only) |

**Where it falls short** (stated in [framework §1](docs/01-framework.md#1-the-decision-in-one-page)):
the JIT fallback meets the approval rule only partly; on GitHub Team nobody sees the prod diff before
apply, so a risk stop holds risky diffs for a second approval; high-risk (L3) changes in deployable
code get one approver, from the owners of the path (process paths get two); admins can edit the
gate (logged, not prevented); "an agent never approves a PR" rests on policy, training and deny
rules that are hygiene, not a technical control; k0s and Firebase are weaker; if the required-check GitHub App is down, every merge is blocked, incident PRs included; whether HIPAA applies is a
legal question.

## How to read it

| You are | Read | Time |
|---|---|---|
| Decision panel | [Executive brief](docs/00-executive-brief.md) (plain language, no codes), [framework §1](docs/01-framework.md#1-the-decision-in-one-page) with the decisions Papaya must take, [diagrams](diagrams/README.md) | ~20 min |
| Compliance | [Compliance register](docs/04-compliance-mapping.md), [threat model](docs/05-threat-model.md), [problem → control map](docs/06-problem-control-map.md) | ~45 min |
| Engineer | [Engineer guide](docs/02-engineer-guide.md), [framework §2](docs/01-framework.md#2-agent-assisted-devsecops-workflows) (how the agents are used), [examples](examples/README.md), framework layers 1–3 | ~45 min |

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| [docs/](docs/) | Executive brief; framework (the decision, agent-assisted workflows, 8 layers: principle, Papaya's stack, audit evidence, cost/value); guide, rollout, register, threat model, map, [framework appendix](docs/07-framework-appendix.md) (detail, gaps, the author's decisions), [ADRs](docs/adr/README.md) |
| [examples/](examples/README.md) | Ruleset, CODEOWNERS, workflows, a runnable risk stop, IAM/OIDC/SCP, managed settings, plugin marketplace, policy pack; each with a local check and what it does **not** prove |
| [diagrams/](diagrams/README.md) | Change workflow, trust boundaries, incident lane |
| [work/](work/) | Working notes and decision log (Vietnamese, with English summaries) |
| [transcripts/](transcripts/) | Complete, raw, unedited Claude Code session files |
| [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) | The rules the agent followed in this repository |

## Evidence markers

Every claim about a tool carries one: ✅ verified here · 📖 official documentation, with a link or a research row `R x.y` in
[work/02-research.md](work/02-research.md) · ⚠️ inference or not verified · [design] my proposal, untested.
Nothing was run against Papaya's systems; I had no access to them.

## How this was built

The repository was written with Claude Code under the same approach it recommends:

- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) set the rules: source markers, no secrets, design only.
- From the research step on, each step went to an **independent reviewer subagent** (given the file
  and the criteria, not my conclusions) until no HIGH/MEDIUM finding remained or the owner stopped the
  rounds; [the log](work/session-log.md) notes fixes that were not re-reviewed. The framing was reviewed with the owner.
- **Deviation:** `CLAUDE.md` planned Manual permission mode from session 2, but the VS Code extension
  started most working sessions in **auto mode** (transcripts record `permissionMode: "auto"`;
  `"default"` only in three short sessions, ✅ grep). Auto mode is allowed by choice (D1), but these
  transcripts do not show Manual-mode prompts. Sessions 1–2 (2026-11-08) used the default config profile; later sessions the clean one.
- Material choices were taken by the author, called "owner" in the documents (OD1–OD21, listed in the [framework appendix](docs/07-framework-appendix.md#r-authors-design-decisions-od-n-2026-11-09); OD22 onwards are the fixes after an independent review, `work/07-review.md`). They are not Papaya sign-offs; the choices left to Papaya are in [framework §1](docs/01-framework.md#1-the-decision-in-one-page).

**Deviation from the agreed form** (framing Q14): there is no Claude Code hook example. The framework
defines no specific hook, and hooks fail open unless set to block (framework layer 2); `allowManagedHooksOnly` is in the managed
settings example instead (owner decision, [work/05-deliverable-plan.md](work/05-deliverable-plan.md) §5 Q6).

## Transcripts

All Claude Code sessions for this challenge were run in this repository. The sessions of
2026-11-08 up to session 2 used the default profile (`~/.claude`); later sessions use a clean profile (`~/.claude-papaya`, see
[work/setup-clean-config.sh](work/setup-clean-config.sh)). Each session is one
`<session-id>.jsonl` file plus an optional `<session-id>/` directory holding subagent
transcripts and large tool results (📖 [Claude directory reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory#cleaned-up-automatically)).
They are copied, unedited, into [transcripts/](transcripts/) before each commit that ends a session:

```bash
for CFG in ~/.claude ~/.claude-papaya; do
  SRC="$CFG/projects/-home-do-hoang-minh-hung-papaya-devsecops-challenge"
  [ -d "$SRC" ] && rsync -a --exclude='memory/' --include='*.jsonl' --include='*/' --include='*/**' "$SRC"/ transcripts/
done
```

Claude Code deletes local transcripts after `cleanupPeriodDays` (⚠️ from the settings reference as read
in an earlier session, not re-checked: default 30 days, minimum 1, cannot be disabled). Both profiles on the machine used for this challenge set it to 365 days.

# 09 — Kiểm docs cho các mục sửa F1–F10

## English summary

- Records the documentation checks made before the fixes in `work/08-fix-proposals.md` (step 1 of
  the agreed process). Four read-only research subagents checked AWS, GitHub/npm/Linear, Claude
  Code and Kubernetes/k0s facts against official documentation on 2026-11-09. Later rounds added
  CI checks on GitHub Team, GCP/Firebase/alerting (R9.5–R9.6), Thailand and Hong Kong law (R9.7)
  and Expo/EAS mobile releases (R9.8) for the follow-up fixes F11–F17.
- Rows are cited in the deliverable as **R9.x** (this file), next to the existing R*x.y* rows of
  `work/02-research.md`. Verdicts: confirmed / partly / contradicted / not found.
- Quotes marked "per fetcher" come from a summarising web fetcher, not a verbatim copy; treat them as
  📖 with that caveat.
- Findings that change a proposal are listed under "Impact on the fixes" for each part.

> Working note. Updated: 2026-11-09 · Status: complete (R9.1–R9.8; the Identity Center resource types used for E16 were read from the AWS Service Reference file `sso.json`, see `work/08-fix-proposals.md`)

---

....
## R9.8 Expo / EAS mobile releases (read 2026-11-09; for F17; docs.expo.dev pages carry no version)

| ID | Topic | Finding | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R9.8.1 | Channel, branch, build | A binary points to one channel, fixed at build time (`eas.json` build profile); a channel points to a branch. From SDK 54 a release build may switch channel at runt
| R9.8.2 | Update to prod users | `eas update --channel production`; builds on that channel with a matching runtime version receive it; gradual rollout with `--rollout-percentage`, changed with `eas u
| R9.8.3 | Rollback, republish | `eas update:republish --destination-channel production` promotes a tested update without a rebuild; `eas update:rollback` (interactive) goes back to an earlier update 
| R9.8.4 | Roles | Owner, Admin, Release Manager, Developer, Runner, Viewer; no custom roles. Developer can build, publish updates and manage credentials unless resources are protected. Per-action mat
| R9.8.5 | Protected channels | `eas channel:protect <name>` (EAS CLI >= 24.0.0): only Release Manager, Admin, Owner may publish, republish, roll back, edit the channel or its rollout. Credentials pro
| R9.8.6 | Tokens | Personal tokens inherit the creator's rights unless "Limit access" is set; robot users cannot log in and hold a role; a robot token is limited only by that role; used as `EXPO_TOKE
| R9.8.7 | OIDC from GitHub | Not mentioned; `expo/expo-github-action` takes a `token` input | not found | same; [expo-github-action](https://github.com/expo/expo-github-action) |
| R9.8.8 | Update code signing | Private key signs the manifest locally (`eas update --private-key-path`); certificate is in the build; the app checks the signature before applying. Production or Ente
| R9.8.9 | Audit log | Actor, entity, action, time; entities include project, user, permission, credentials, hosting deployment; Enterprise only; `eas account:audit <account> --json`; kept 1.5 years, 
| R9.8.10 | GitHub Action | `expo/expo-github-action` inputs `token`, `eas-version`, `packager`, `eas-cache`; examples run `eas update --auto --non-interactive` on push to main | confirmed | [expo-git
| R9.8.11 | EAS Workflows | Own `on: push` trigger via Expo's GitHub app; jobs run with at most Developer rights, so they cannot publish to a protected channel | confirmed | [workflows](https://docs.e
| R9.8.12 | Submit, store keys | Non-interactive submit uses keys assigned in EAS (Google service-account key stored on the Expo account) or local key paths in `eas.json`; store-side roles not in thes
| R9.8.13 | Store review, phased rollout | Android submit defaults to the internal track; `releaseStatus: draft` lets a person finish the release in Play Console. Apple/Google roles and phased release
| R9.8.14 | SSO, 2FA | OIDC-based SSO on Production or Enterprise plan; offboarding manual; 2FA per user, no org enforcement documented | partly | [SSO](https://docs.expo.dev/accounts/sso/), [2FA](htt

Impact on F17:

- Technical control: protect the `production` channel and credentials; no human holds Release
  Manager or above day to day; CI publishes with a robot user (Release Manager) whose token sits in
  the `production` environment of GitHub, so only a merged `main` run reaches it.
- Limits: no OIDC, so the robot token is a long-lived secret (secrets inventory, rotation); Owner and
  Admin can remove protection; EAS Workflows cannot publish to a protected channel, so prod goes
  through GitHub Actions and Expo's GitHub app is not connected for prod triggers.
- Code signing (paid plan) is the strongest control: a stolen Expo token cannot ship an update
  without the private key. Key in the `production` environment; KMS signing ⚠️ not documented.
- Detection without Enterprise audit log: reconcile updates on the `production` channel against
  deploy runs and merged commits (evidence export).
- Rollback is a protected action: in the incident lane it runs as a reviewed PR/re-run of the

# Kubernetes API audit policy for prod k0s (framework layer 7; OD24) [design].
# k0s ships with no audit policy (R9.3.2); it is enabled through spec.api.extraArgs
# (k0s-apiserver-audit.yaml), which is outside k0s support (R9.3.1).
# Levels (R9.3.3): Metadata = who, verb, resource, no bodies. Secrets, ConfigMaps and token
# requests stay at Metadata so their contents never reach the audit log. Writes to workloads
# and RBAC are kept at Request, so a change can be compared with the merged manifests.
# ⚠️ Rule order: from memory, the first matching rule sets the level; check the audit page.
apiVersion: audit.k8s.io/v1
kind: Policy
omitStages: ["RequestReceived"]
rules:
  - level: Metadata

# Fragment of k0s.yaml on every controller (OD24) [design]. spec.api.extraArgs passes flags to
# kube-apiserver; "Any behavior triggered by these parameters is outside k0s support" (R9.3.1).
# The policy file must be placed on each controller by Papaya (no k0s mechanism found, R9.3.2);
# shipping the log to the log-archive account is part of gap G1.
apiVersion: k0s.k0sproject.io/v1beta1
kind: ClusterConfig
spec:
  api:
    extraArgs:
      audit-policy-file: /etc/k0s/audit-policy.yaml
      audit-log-path: /var/log/k0s/audit.log
      audit-log-maxage: "30"

# Interim k0s deploy credential (framework layer 5, exception OD1/OD6; owner decision OD24)
# [design]. One ServiceAccount per deploy namespace, bound to a namespaced Role. Its token is
# time-limited (`kubectl create token ci-deploy -n claims --duration=720h`; the server may
# shorten it, R9.3.6) and stored only in the `production-k0s` environment of GitHub.
#
# Not granted on purpose (R9.3.7): Secrets (get/list/watch all reveal contents), pods/exec,
# pods/log, serviceaccounts/token, roles/rolebindings (escalate, bind), impersonate,
# nodes/proxy (bypasses audit logging), deletes. Workload deletes and RBAC changes go through the
# L3 owner team with a separate credential. Caveat (R9.3.7): creating a workload grants it the
# API access of any ServiceAccount in the namespace, so deploy namespaces hold no privileged
# ServiceAccount.
apiVersion: v1

# Kubernetes API audit policy for prod k0s (framework layer 7; OD24) [design].
# k0s ships with no audit policy (R9.3.2); it is enabled through spec.api.extraArgs
# (k0s-apiserver-audit.yaml), which is outside k0s support (R9.3.1).
# Levels (R9.3.3): Metadata = who, verb, resource, no bodies. Secrets, ConfigMaps and token
# requests stay at Metadata so their contents never reach the audit log. Writes to workloads
# and RBAC are kept at Request, so a change can be compared with the merged manifests.
# ⚠️ Rule order: from memory, the first matching rule sets the level; check the audit page.
apiVersion: audit.k8s.io/v1
kind: Policy
omitStages: ["RequestReceived"]
rules:
  - level: Metadata

# Fragment of k0s.yaml on every controller (OD24) [design]. spec.api.extraArgs passes flags to
# kube-apiserver; "Any behavior triggered by these parameters is outside k0s support" (R9.3.1).
# The policy file must be placed on each controller by Papaya (no k0s mechanism found, R9.3.2);
# shipping the log to the log-archive account is part of gap G1.
apiVersion: k0s.k0sproject.io/v1beta1
kind: ClusterConfig
spec:
  api:
    extraArgs:
      audit-policy-file: /etc/k0s/audit-policy.yaml
      audit-log-path: /var/log/k0s/audit.log
      audit-log-maxage: "30"

# Interim k0s deploy credential (framework layer 5, exception OD1/OD6; owner decision OD24)
# [design]. One ServiceAccount per deploy namespace, bound to a namespaced Role. Its token is
# time-limited (`kubectl create token ci-deploy -n claims --duration=720h`; the server may
# shorten it, R9.3.6) and stored only in the `production-k0s` environment of GitHub.
#
# Not granted on purpose (R9.3.7): Secrets (get/list/watch all reveal contents), pods/exec,
# pods/log, serviceaccounts/token, roles/rolebindings (escalate, bind), impersonate,
# nodes/proxy (bypasses audit logging), deletes. Workload deletes and RBAC changes go through the
# L3 owner team with a separate credential. Caveat (R9.3.7): creating a workload grants it the
# API access of any ServiceAccount in the namespace, so deploy namespaces hold no privileged
# ServiceAccount.
apiVersion: v1

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Prod environments, their secrets and variables (names only)

Every prod environment uses the same settings as `environment.json` and `branch-policy.json`
here: deployments from `main` only, no required reviewers (not available on GitHub Team for
private repos). Secrets are set through the environment-secrets REST API or the settings UI, never
as repository secrets, and never stored in git. Framework layers 1 and 5; OD1, OD6, OD22, OD24,
OD36, OD40.

| Environment | Used by | OIDC trust (examples/aws/) | Secrets |
|---|---|---|---|
| `production` | `deploy-prod.yml`, domain stacks (Pulumi, Serverless) | `oidc-trust-prod-deploy.json` | none |
| `production-iam` | `deploy-prod.yml`, stack `iam` only (OD22) | `oidc-trust-prod-iam-deploy.json` | none |
| `production-db` | `deploy-prod.yml`, tool `sql` only (ADR-0011) | `oidc-trust-prod-db-change.json` | none |
| `production-k0s` | the k0s and Firebase deploy workflow only (OD24) | the k0s API trusts this subject in the target design (`examples/k0s/authentication-config.target.yaml`) | `K0S_DEPLOY_TOKEN`, `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY` |
| `production-mobile` | the mobile release workflow only (OD40) | none: Expo has no OIDC for GitHub (R9.8.7) | `EXPO_ROBOT_TOKEN`, `EAS_UPDATE_SIGNING_KEY` |

Secrets, all S2 exceptions with an owner, an expiry and a rotation in the exception register:

| Secret | What it is | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| `K0S_DEPLOY_TOKEN` | Time-limited token of the namespaced deploy ServiceAccount (`examples/k0s/deploy-rbac.yaml`), not a kubeconfig | Until the k0s API trusts GitHub OIDC (OD24, G1) |
| `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY` | Service-account JSON key for Firebase Hosting deploys; the official action needs one (R9.6.5) | Until the WIF spike shows `firebase deploy` works without a key (OD36, G2) |
| `EXPO_ROBOT_TOKEN` | Access token of the Expo robot user with the Release Manager role | Expo has no keyless login from GitHub (R9.8.7) |
| `EAS_UPDATE_SIGNING_KEY` | Private key that signs EAS updates (R9.8.8) | Lives only here, so a stolen Expo token alone cannot ship code |

A separate environment per secret holder means jobs of the AWS deploy workflow cannot read them,
and each environment is referenced by one workflow file (all under CODEOWNERS, L3). On
self-hosted runners environment secrets act like repository secrets (R3.1.5), so these jobs run
on GitHub-hosted runners.

Environment **variables** (prod-only, kept on the environment rather than the repository):
`AWS_REGION`, `PROD_PULUMI_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN`, `PROD_SERVERLESS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN` on `production`
and `production-iam`; `PROD_DB_CHANGE_ROLE_ARN` on `production-db`; `PULUMI_BACKEND_URL`,
`PULUMI_CLI_VERSION`, `NODE_VERSION`. They are read by `workflows/deploy-prod.yml` only.

# Kubernetes API audit policy for prod k0s (framework layer 7; OD24) [design].
# k0s ships with no audit policy (R9.3.2); it is enabled through spec.api.extraArgs
# (k0s-apiserver-audit.yaml), which is outside k0s support (R9.3.1).
# Levels (R9.3.3): Metadata = who, verb, resource, no bodies. Secrets, ConfigMaps and token
# requests stay at Metadata so their contents never reach the audit log. Writes to workloads
# and RBAC are kept at Request, so a change can be compared with the merged manifests.
# ⚠️ Rule order: from memory, the first matching rule sets the level; check the audit page.
apiVersion: audit.k8s.io/v1
kind: Policy
omitStages: ["RequestReceived"]
rules:
  - level: Metadata
    resources:
      - group: ""
        resources: ["secrets", "configmaps", "serviceaccounts/token"]
  - level: Request
    verbs: ["create", "update", "patch", "delete", "deletecollection"]
    resources:
      - group: "apps"
      - group: "batch"
      - group: "rbac.authorization.k8s.io"
  - level: Metadata

# Interim k0s deploy credential (framework layer 5, exception OD1/OD6; owner decision OD24)
# [design]. One ServiceAccount per deploy namespace, bound to a namespaced Role. Its token is
# time-limited (`kubectl create token ci-deploy -n claims --duration=720h`; the server may
# shorten it, R9.3.6) and stored only in the `production-k0s` environment of GitHub.
#
# Not granted on purpose (R9.3.7): Secrets (get/list/watch all reveal contents), pods/exec,
# pods/log, serviceaccounts/token, roles/rolebindings (escalate, bind), impersonate,
# nodes/proxy (bypasses audit logging), deletes. Workload deletes and RBAC changes go through the
# L3 owner team with a separate credential. Caveat (R9.3.7): creating a workload grants it the
# API access of any ServiceAccount in the namespace, so deploy namespaces hold no privileged
# ServiceAccount.
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: ci-deploy
  namespace: claims
automountServiceAccountToken: false
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: ci-deploy
  namespace: claims
rules:
  - apiGroups: ["apps"]
    resources: ["deployments", "statefulsets"]
    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch", "create", "update", "patch"]
  - apiGroups: ["batch"]
    resources: ["jobs", "cronjobs"]
    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch", "create", "update", "patch"]
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: ["services", "configmaps"]
    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch", "create", "update", "patch"]
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: ["pods"]
    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]  # rollout status only
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: ci-deploy
  namespace: claims
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: Role
  name: ci-deploy
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: ci-deploy
    namespace: claims

- `work/10-verify.md` đã cập nhật những chỗ cũ (summary, V7, V13, §6.3–6.4).
